worked_solution:
The sum formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =1 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\  & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={2}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =4+4 \\ {R}^{2} & =8 \\ R & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x+{45}^{∘})
$$
